rows.name: validate:citation-repair-reach
rows.risk_prevented: A citation-contract repair that cannot reach the pages its own validator judges. repair_schema_parity.py honoured data/release/active_mutation_scope.json (~17 routes) while validate_citation_contract.py judged all 2219 ACTIVE citable pages, so a page that lost CITATION_PAGE_SCHEMA outside the release scope was unrepairable by construction: heal_until_clean.mjs re-ran the same repair every attempt, changed nothing relevant, and exited UNRESOLVED. Production run 33259007622 shows 'changed=18; scoped=True; skipped_outside_scope=2183' followed by FAIL on three pages none of the 18 included, and the Spry Content Release lane stayed red on it.

rows.name: validate:demand-backed-pages
rows.risk_prevented: A page published with no measured demand behind it, a sitemap URL that does not render, and a page admitted at 'baseline' - the level that skips word count, unique artifact, worked example, source floor and unique_atom strength in validate_programmatic_admission.py. The validator existed and was in no profile, so nothing ran it.

rows.name: validate:search-measurement-truthfulness
rows.risk_prevented: Prevents the search-measurement lane from reporting zeros while calling itself healthy: an all-zero GSC dataset marked OK, a target-query filter that discards every returned row in silence, URL Inspection verdicts discarded after being paid for, an ingest failure swallowed by `|| true`, and a sitemap lastmod that is either stale or stamped with build time.

rows.name: validate:citation-signal-join
rows.risk_prevented: Prevents competition_opportunity - a weighted, declared scoring input - from silently measuring nothing while looking like it works. The citation lookup was keyed on a scalar `query` that a cluster record does not have (it carries a nested queries[]), so all 120 clusters recorded "this query has not been probed" while 83 grounded observations sat unused, and the engine correctly dropped the component and redistributed its weight, which made a 100% failure indistinguishable from normal operation. Also prevents "a grounded answer cited nobody of ours" being scored as maximum open ground for a brand or navigational query ("sprylabs", "spry reddit"), and requires the run to disclose how much of the component was actually measured.

rows.name: validate:no-silent-zero-work
rows.risk_prevented: Prevents any lane from exiting 0 while having produced no work. Guards the exact defects found in this audit: the zero-dollar citation plan discarding 100% of its candidates behind a permanently-disabled fixture gate while printing PASS; the apply stage hardcoding status PASS with release_units_applied=0; the strategy gap-fill lane queueing 10 candidates a day that no consumer ever turns into files; the answer-surface scorer reading a file nothing writes while the real citation probe wrote elsewhere; the admin dashboard rendering a stalled zero identically to a healthy day; the search-intelligence lane re-observing the same 24 of 120 targets forever; and validate_fanout_warning hardcoding status PASS with 3110 findings.

rows.name: validate:lastmod-ledger-final
rows.risk_prevented: Prevents a sitemap lastmod ledger being committed that does not describe the tree it ships with. The ledger was derived part-way through a release, later stages rewrote the pages it had just hashed, and it was committed alongside them: at 6aac79a2e the committed ledger contradicted 1,900 of 2,223 committed pages. Nothing failed where the bad ledger was produced; it surfaced days later as an 8-URL sample mismatch inside sitemap:lastmod:self-test, on branches that had cut from main and inherited the failure as if it were their own. This asserts the committed ledger against every committed page, refuses a freshly derived ledger that already disagrees with the tree, and statically requires every content-release mode to derive the ledger as its final stage.

rows.name: validate:ledger-receipt-run-scope
rows.risk_prevented: Prevents a lastmod derivation receipt inherited from the commit being read as proof that THIS run derived the ledger. The receipt lives under artifacts/, which the main-writing lanes commit, so from 93977956f (2026-09-03 12:58Z) every checkout began with a receipt already hashing to the ledger beside it. Spry Content Release run 33767079923 never executed sitemap:lastmod:content - full-content-cycle derives the ledger as its last stage and the lane fails at selfheal, the stage before it - yet arm B of validate:lastmod-ledger-final believed a derivation had happened, compared the untouched committed ledger to a working tree the release stages had rewritten, and reported 1590 of 2231 pages stale. Nothing was stale. Self-heal correctly refused to repair it and the scheduled lane paged its owner every day. Both doors are held: ledgerDerivationReceipt refuses a receipt byte-identical to the one at HEAD, which protects every tree that already carries a committed one; .gitignore plus a narrowed staging pathspec in commit_and_push_if_changed.sh stop new ones being committed at all. The staging exclusion is deliberately limited to artifacts/validation/*receipt*.json, because most of that directory IS read across runs - pre-implementation-protected-hashes.json, workflow-yaml-inventory.json, daily-citation-release-plan.json and internal-navigation-structure.json all have readers with no fallback - so a blanket exclusion would freeze inputs and let the release exit 0 having published nothing.

rows.name: validate:build-cache-integrity
rows.risk_prevented: Guards scripts/build/ (the content-hash cache wrapping `npm run build:all`, docs/runbooks/BUILD_CACHE.md). Prevents a cache entry existing for a build that never reached exit 0, an entry with a non-empty diff and no payload to restore, a stale payload sitting next to a claimed empty-diff (fixed-point) entry, and the safety invariants in cached_build_all.sh/save_build_cache.mjs/restore_build_cache.mjs being weakened without a validator noticing. This is the exact class of defect that produced FROZEN_OUTPUT_MATERIAL_SHRINK on 2026-09-01: a snapshot taken from a tree build_navigation_structure.mjs and build:visible-faq had not finished writing to yet.

rows.name: validate:admin-command-verify
rows.risk_prevented: Keeps the Admin Command workflow provable without turning it red, and keeps its three copies of the command list in agreement. The workflow's only run ever - 33274444603 on 2026-08-29, event=workflow_dispatch - was an audit dispatching action __parse_probe__ with reason 'audit parse probe'. The workflow was healthy; run_admin_command.mjs threw because __parse_probe__ was not a registered command, so confirming the lane worked is what made it fail, and that failure stayed the latest status of an ACTIVE workflow. There was no green way to probe it: every registered command mutated data/admin/runtime_control.json and was committed to main. This asserts that a read-only command exists, is offered by the dispatch dropdown, exits 0 having actually examined the registered commands and the control state, writes nothing, and is gated out of the commit step; and that the mutating commands still work.

rows.name: validate:workflow-manual-only-declared
rows.risk_prevented: Admin Operations has never run on main and nothing in the repository could say whether that was deliberate or whether the lane had silently died; 'never ran' looks identical for a workflow nobody needed to dispatch and a workflow everyone forgot. This reconciles every trigger-less workflow against data/workflows/manual_only_workflows.json in both directions, so a manual-only lane must state why it is manual and a declaration that has gone stale fails on the trigger, not on the wording. It also fails a dispatch dropdown that no step gates on and no script reads, which would let every option exit 0 having done nothing the operator asked for.

rows.name: validate:risk-statement-substance
rows.risk_prevented: A HARD_FAIL gate whose risk_prevented is the tool's placeholder cannot be reviewed: nobody reading the registry can tell what it refuses, and audit_governance_blockers.mjs reads that same field when proposing a severity migration. This refuses any new record carrying the placeholder, and ratchets the 53 that predate the rule so the list can only shrink.
